This piece of Russian propaganda tries to separate Ukraine from its European supporters.</li> <li><a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/the-us-wants-to-disintegrate-the-eu-through-the-war-in-ukraine/"><em>The US wants to disintegrate the EU through the war in Ukraine</em></a>. No, it does not. This is a recurring pro-Kremlin narrative attempting to drive a wedge between transatlantic partners by insinuating that the US would somehow benefit from the war in Ukraine.</li> </ul> <p><img class="alignnone size-full wp-image-142559" src="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/uploads/2022/11/NOV15_3.png" alt="" width="1600" height="900" /></p> ","link":"https://euvsdisinfo.eu/the-little-tractor-that-could/"},{"type":"article","title":"Behind the curtain: a novel analytical approach to FIMI exposure","content":"<p>The European External Action Service (EEAS) has released its third report on foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) threats. <strong>Read the full report <a href="https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/3rd-eeas-report-foreign-information-manipulation-and-interference-threats-0_en" target="_blank" rel="noopener">here</a></strong>.</p> <p>Like <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/time-to-take-a-step-forward-from-analysis-to-a-collective-response/">previous reports</a>, the latest iteration of the report is based on carefully collected data of observed FIMI activity, to identify and analyse the key trends in 2024. Building on the guidance provided by last year’s report on moving toward collective response, the 3<sup>rd</sup> report on FIMI threats introduces a novel element to analyse foreign information manipulation and interference – the FIMI Exposure Matrix, which was applied to analyse a sample of 505 FIMI incidents involving some 38 000 channels engaged in information manipulation.</p> <p><img class="alignnone size-medium wp-image-196722" src="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/uploads/2025/03/key-trends-600x233.png" alt="Infographic showing key figures of 2024 incidents." width="600" height="233" /></p> <p>EU High Representative of Foreign Affairs and Security Policy/ Vice-President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas presented the report and stated clearly that the threat of FIMI is global and must not be underestimated, because ‘the aim [of FIMI] is to destabilise our societies, damage our democracies, drive wedges between us and our partners and undermine the EU’s global standing.’</p> <h3><strong>Russia and China continue to adapt their FIMI operations</strong></h3> <p>Like previous years, Russia and China remain among the most prolific FIMI threat actors, their tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs) characterised by continuous adaptation both to harness new and emerging technologies and to circumvent the restrictive measures imposed against them. In this context the use of artificial intelligence has become more frequent in 2024, both to enable and facilitate content creation, including for large Russian state-run FIMI actors <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/how-russia-uses-ai-to-dehumanise-ukrainians/">like RIA Novosti</a>, and to <strong>enable automatisation</strong> and the <strong>scaling-up</strong> of content distribution.</p> <p>For the Kremlin, FIMI, or the weaponisation of information, is a tool to advance Russia’s geopolitical objectives and, in 2024, can be characterised as an attempt to <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/building-a-false-facade/">build a False Façade</a> to hide pro-Kremlin information laundering operations. Russia sought to exploit specific local vulnerabilities with carefully tailored and targeted content, especially zeroing in on elections around the globe. However, <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/ukraine/"><strong>undermining Ukraine</strong></a> and Western support to it remained at the forefront of Russia’s FIMI operations in 2024, as it has for <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/what-we-have-learnt-about-fimi-after-three-years-of-full-scale-war-in-ukraine/">the three years of Russia’s full-scale war</a> in Ukraine.</p> <p>China continued to expand its state-controlled media footprint globally as it deployed multiple FIMI tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), from classic information manipulation operations to supressing critical voices. Notably, China’s FIMI proxies extend beyond the state-run media enterprise, co-opting private PR companies and influencers to broaden geographic and linguistic coverage, often with the aim of concealing origin and affiliation.</p> <p>In 2024, China’s FIMI activities continued to operate alongside other threat actors, including Russia, but the cross pollination between Russian and Chinese FIMI ecosystems seems to remain largely opportunistic. However, in terms of narratives, there was a significant convergence on messaging blaming NATO for escalating conflict with Russia.</p> <h3><strong>Elections in the </strong><strong>crosshairs</strong></h3> <p>Based on the sampled 505 FIMI incidents, it is evident that FIMI is a global threat with significant local implications, particularly in the context of elections, both within the EU and globally. For example, Russian FIMI actors systematically targeted the <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/european-elections/">European elections</a> in 2024, escalating activity in the weeks leading up the elections and continuing well beyond them.</p> <p>Outside the EU, <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/moldova/">Moldova</a> was heavily targeted by Russian FIMI activity. The October–November 2024 presidential elections and the EU membership referendum in Moldova revealed a significant escalation in Russia’s FIMI operations. Russia used a complex, multi-layered, and adaptive FIMI infrastructure. These operations strategically combined existing infrastructure with newly developed assets and campaigns to influence and manipulate voter behaviour. Notably, Russian FIMI infrastructure previously used against Ukraine was redeployed to attack Moldova, adapting networks and narratives to a new front of interference.</p> <p>Of course, pro-Kremlin attempts to meddle in elections go beyond the incidents sampled in the report. As we have observed and exposed on the <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/disinformation-cases/">EUvsDisinfo database</a>, elections in <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/tainting-the-new-dawn/">France</a> and <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/pro-kremlin-outlets-drool-over-german-elections/">Germany</a> were also frequently in the Kremlin’s crosshairs.</p> <h3><strong>Echoes of Russian FIMI influence in Africa</strong></h3> <p>Russia’s FIMI infrastructure in <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/africa/">Africa</a> in 2024 reflects a long-term, multi-layered strategy developed over recent years. In Africa, the Kremlin has also capitalised on regional political shifts, aiming to position itself as a counterpower to the West. As shown in the report, Russia has grown its state-controlled media presence, e.g. by expanding the RT and Sputnik networks, but has also adapted and grown its covert influence networks, such as the <a href="https://www.lemonde.fr/en/le-monde-africa/article/2024/03/09/african-initiative-the-new-bridgehead-for-russian-propaganda-in-africa_6599556_124.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">African Initiative</a>.</p> <p><img class="alignnone size-medium wp-image-196718" src="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/uploads/2025/03/fimi-africa-600x333.png" alt="" width="600" height="333" /></p> <h3><strong>The tip of the FIMI iceberg</strong></h3> <p>So, how do we know what we know? Because the EEAS has deployed the proposed FIMI Exposure Matrix to uncover the iceberg that epitomises the FIMI architecture. The iceberg analogy is not accidental because much like an iceberg, FIMI architecture can have a more visible part and an often larger, hidden part. Threat actors like Russia and China deploy covert infrastructure to enable their FIMI operations by creating hidden networks that infiltrate local audiences and deliver deceptive narratives. The covert character of these manipulative efforts indicates that FIMI is a hybrid activity.</p> <p>The FIMI Exposure Matrix is composed of four categories. Three can attributed to a threat actor: 1) official state channels; 2) state-controlled outlets; and 3) state-linked channels. The fourth category cannot be necessarily attributed to a state actor, but these entities still play a significant role in FIMI activities as they show a systematic alignment and similar behaviour characteristics.</p> <p><img class="alignnone size-medium wp-image-196720" src="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/uploads/2025/03/iceberg-600x582.png" alt="" width="600" height="582" /></p> <p>Each of these four categories are characterised by specific behavioural and technical indicators. Understanding the modus operandi of each category is crucial to defining and exposing them as FIMI entities. Technical indicators may include public affiliation (and even self-attribution), as well as financial records revealing the sources of funding, and evidence of shared IT infrastructure. Behavioural evidence may include amplification patterns (e.g. mirroring content, automated translations, republishing), as well as using inauthentic AI generated accounts, coordinated messaging and branding similarities. Based on this approach, it is possible to infer a more comprehensive understanding of the role and function various entities play in the overall FIMI architecture.</p> <p><img class="alignnone size-medium wp-image-196721" src="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/uploads/2025/03/iceberg_outlets-600x541.png" alt="" width="600" height="541" /></p> <p>The EEAS has been building a comprehensive approach to mitigate the threat of information manipulation. The <a href="https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/1st-eeas-report-foreign-information-manipulation-and-interference-threats_en" target="_blank" rel="noopener">first report on FIMI threats</a>, published in 2023, focussed on how to analyse information manipulation and introduced the FIMI methodology, a <strong>groundbreaking step</strong> to <strong>standardise the approach</strong> to FIMI investigations. The <a href="https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/2nd-eeas-report-foreign-information-manipulation-and-interference-threats_en" target="_blank" rel="noopener">next iteration of the report</a> used the methodology to propose a <strong>collective response framework</strong> to FIMI threats. Now, the third report takes a step further by detailing a <strong>practical approach to exposure and attribution</strong> – a much needed step to safeguard our democracies in increasingly tumultuous times. <a href="https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/3rd-eeas-report-foreign-information-manipulation-and-interference-threats-0_en" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read the report</a>, learn more, and don’t be deceived.</p> ","link":"https://euvsdisinfo.eu/behind-the-curtain-a-novel-analytical-approach-to-fimi-exposure/"},{"type":"article","title":"Figure of the Week: 5","content":"<p>Polish authorities issue 5-year entry bans against five alleged Russian ‘information war’ operatives involved in stoking Polish-Ukrainian animosity.</p> <p>According to the public news agency <a href="http://www.thenews.pl/1/9/Artykul/363985,UPDATE-Poland-cracks-down-on-%E2%80%98Russian-hybrid-war%E2%80%99-campaign" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Informacyjna Agencja Radiowa</a>, two women, identified only as Yekaterina C. and Anastasia Z., were detained last week on allegations of involvement in ‘hybrid warfare’ activities.</p> <p>A spokesperson for the Polish Internal Security Agency (ABW) stated that, along with the two detained persons, three other foreign citizens were handed 5-year bans on entering Poland, being accused of engaging in non-military influence operations aimed at furthering foreign interests. The ABW claimed to have ‘successfully neutralized’ two networks involved in promoting Russian interpretations of history with the aim to sow discord between Poles and Ukrainians in South-Eastern Poland. The investigation also targeted Polish citizens who had allegedly received funds and direct instructions from ‘Russian institutions <a href="https://twitter.com/StZaryn/status/997506763283890176" target="_blank" rel="noopener">closely linked</a> to the […] authorities of the Russian Federation’.</p> <p>For years, Poland has been a strong supporter of Ukraine’s Western aspirations, as well as of sanctions resulting from Russia’s intervention in Crimea and Eastern Ukraine. Recently, however, social media in Poland has witnessed an increasingly assertive <a href="https://www.thedailybeast.com/russias-covert-campaign-inflaming-east-europe" target="_blank" rel="noopener">disinformation campaign</a> aiming to revisit and distort complex and controversial historical events and making use of already existing tensions inflamed by local nationalist, far-right groups.</p> <p>Revision of history has been a recurrent tactic in the toolbox of pro-Kremlin disinformation campaigns, with the aim of inflaming potentially contentious issues between neighbouring states or ethnic groups. See such past examples already covered in our database:</p> <p><a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/czechoslovakia-should-be-grateful-to-the-ussr-for-1968/" rel="noopener">“Czechoslovakia should be grateful to the USSR for 1968”</a></p> <p><a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/in-1801-georgia-joined-russia-of-its-own-free-will/" rel="noopener">In 1801, Georgia joined Russia of its own free will</a></p> <p><a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/exploiting-commemorations/" rel="noopener">Exploiting commemorations</a></p> ","link":"https://euvsdisinfo.eu/figure-of-the-week-5/"},{"type":"article","title":"The Bucha massacre: How to deflect attention in Poland","content":"<p>On 4-5 April, when the news of the Russian massacres in Bucha outside Kyiv hit international media (but not in Russia!), Poland faced a large-scale troll attack, which had at least three dimensions:</p> <ul> <li>threatening emails sent to Polish decision-makers</li> <li>spam attack on Polish media</li> <li>boosting of the World War II Volyn massacre issue on Polish social media.</li> </ul> <p>This way, the Russian trolls once again tried to undermine Polish support for Ukraine.</p> <h3><strong>Threats to decision-makers</strong></h3> <p>Hundreds of Polish <a href="https://nowysacz.naszemiasto.pl/sadecka-posel-elzbieta-zielinska-dostala-maila-z-grozbami/ar/c1-8760019" target="_blank" rel="noopener">politicians</a>, public figures, journalists and experts received an <a href="https://www.o2.pl/informacje/atak-trolli-na-polskich-politykow-za-ukraine-ludzie-to-interes-polski-6754978230418016a?fbclid=IwAR2mSpUKo0XgK50BfbLoFuSkWlImri6edeo6GLIQJgd6wXB-u74amAjP5O4" target="_blank" rel="noopener">email</a> from a “Polish patriot” who threatened to kill them in the most brutal way for their support of the “Banderite Ukraine”. “Banderite” is shorthand for <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/disinformation-cases/?disinfo_keywords%5B0%5D=keyword_77254&offset=10">Stephan Bandera</a>, a Ukrainian politician, Nazi collaborator and theorist of the militant wing of the far-right Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists. <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/during-german-occupation-of-ukraine-the-nazi-bandera-contributed-to-the-genocide-of-his-own-people/">References to Bandera</a> form a recurring pro-Kramlin narrative aimed at denying Ukriane’s identity and equating Ukrainian nationalism with Nazism. Bandera is also a controversial figure in Poland, to say the least, for his anti-Polish stance. Bandera has been used by the Kremlin disinformation machine many times <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/disinformation-cases/?text=bandera&date=&per_page=/">before</a>, in an attempt to touch on the most painful elements of Polish-Ukrainian history.</p> <p>The text of this email was written in quite a primitive way, so it was evident to the recipients that it was an unsophisticated troll attack rather than a serious death threat.</p> <h3><strong>Spam attack on Polish media </strong></h3> <p>On 5 April, at least one large Polish media agency was bombarded with <a href="https://twitter.com/chojecka_kasia/status/1511312363206631426" target="_blank" rel="noopener">emails</a> from “regular Russians” who tried to convince the Polish media and journalists that “Nazi” Ukraine committed <a href="https://twitter.com/chojecka_kasia/status/1511337401016360972" target="_blank" rel="noopener">war crimes</a> against Russian soldiers. These emails were written both in English and Polish.</p> <h3><strong>The Volyn Massacre trending on Twitter</strong></h3> <p>Also starting 4-5 April, the topic of the <a href="https://www.thefirstnews.com/article/over-100000-slaughtered-with-axes-pitchforks-scythes-and-knives-the-wolyn-massacre-started-76-years-ago-today-and-lasted-for-two-years-6714" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Volyn massacre</a> entered the list of top trends on Polish Twitter.</p> <p>The Volyn Massacre is one of the most painful episodes in relations between the peoples of Poland and Ukraine. The tragedy took place throughout 1943-1944 when tens of thousands of Poles living in the Volyn and Galicia regions were murdered or expelled by Ukrainian militia forces.</p> <p>Polish historiography presents this as an act of genocide or a series of large-scale massacres against the Poles committed by Ukrainian nationalists at that time.</p> <p>Ukrainian historiography presents it as two-side ethnic cleansing taking place during the military conflict between the Polish and Ukrainian militia forces throughout WWII.</p> <h3><strong>Why now?</strong></h3> <p>Why bringing the topic up now? The Volyn massacre happened almost eighty years ago, but it remains a painful memory for many. And it has been exploited by the Kremlin before, be it for historical <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/the-polish-legions-of-pilsudski-organized-the-volyn-tragedy/">revisionism</a> or to repeat well-know manipulation tropes on <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/ukraine-is-a-nazi-state-kiev-is-preparing-to-repeat/">Nazis</a> ruling Ukraine.</p> <p>It is hardly a coincidence that the tragedy was highlighted again at this point in time, exactly when the details about the Bucha massacre and Russia’s responsibility for this war crime started appearing in international media.</p> <p>The trend “Volyn massacre” on Polish Twitter was initiated or at least boosted by the Russian troll networks; after 5 April, it disappeared. A major part of the posts on this topic was published by Polish Twitter users with strong far-right and anti-Ukrainian views, but they did not have enough weight to dominate Twitter trends. An artificial “helping hand”, or to be more precise, coordinated inauthentic behaviour, including malign use of bots and artificial intelligence, was at play. Such use is a standard tool in the Kremlin <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/think-before-you-share/">playbook</a>.</p> <h3><strong>The messages to Poland </strong></h3> <p>Pro-Kremlin narratives circulating in the Polish information environment underlined a few messages: that the Ukrainians will finally understand the Polish pain from the Ukrainian genocide against the Poles during WWII; that the Ukrainians massacred Poles during WWII and now face retaliation from the Russians; that the Ukrainians refused to recognise the Volyn Massacre as genocide, so now they have to suffer from the Russian actions; that the Bucha events are not a real genocide since the Volyn massacre was one hundred times bigger; that the Poles should remember the historical Ukrainian crimes despite the Russian attack on Ukraine; that the Ukrainians keep praising Bandera and other persons responsible for the anti-Polish actions, so now, they face the consequences of such a position.</p> <p>In other words, trolls and anonymous bots tried to draw parallels between Bucha and Volyn as well as underline Ukraine’s responsibility for the Volyn massacre as an argument that Ukrainians have no moral right to call the Bucha events a genocide. All that in an attempt to divert attention from Russia’s crimes and to drive a wedge between Ukrainians and Poles, who during the current war became closer than ever.</p> <h3><strong>Disinformation campaign in full swing</strong></h3> <p>The disinformation and manipulation campaign was not only rather primitive and clumsy; moreover, it did not take into consideration the current mood in Polish society.</p> <p>The current situation obviously annoys the Kremlin – as 2.6 million Ukrainian refugees entered Poland since Russia attacked Ukraine again, and the wave of <a href="https://www.dw.com/en/polands-open-door-policy-helps-ukrainian-refugees-build-new-lives/a-61192590#:~:text=Poland's%20open%2Ddoor%20policy%20helps,people%20arriving%20in%20the%20country." target="_blank" rel="noopener">help</a> and welcome from Polish citizens is historic, in spite of the magnitude of the challenge.</p> <p>While the Russian war machine try to bomb more Ukrainians to flee their homes, the Kremlin’s disinformation machine will likely keep trying to drive further wedges, feed on difficult topics, use tropes of racism, xenophobia and painful divisive events from the past, as it did <a href="https://oko.press/rosja-wybiela-sie-z-kramatorska-i-buczy-czesc-polakow-w-to-wierzy/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">before</a>.</p> ","link":"https://euvsdisinfo.eu/the-bucha-massacre-how-to-deflect-attention-in-poland/"},{"type":"article","title":"The Kremlin prepares for the Polish EU presidency","content":"<p>As Poland prepares to take on the presidency of the EU Council on 1 January 2025, it continues to face intense disinformation attacks from top-level Russian officials and pro-Kremlin outlets.</p> <p>Much of the Russian disinformation spread by the Polish edition of Pravda throughout 2024 can be summarised by three narratives. Firstly, Poland is an aggressive Western puppet. Secondly, it has strong imperialist ambitions. Thirdly, it wants nothing but war</p> <h3><strong>Poland as an aggressive Western puppet</strong></h3> <p>Russian state and pro-Kremlin outlets have consistently presented Poland as a US-controlled ‘puppet’ with no sovereignty. Specifically, Washington and NATO have used Poland as an aggressive anti-Russian actor and a ‘barking <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-and-the-baltic-states-are-natos-barking-chain-dogs/">chain dog</a>’. Examples have included: Poland behaves like an obedient <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-behaves-like-a-51st-state-of-the-usa/">51st state</a> of the US, the <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/the-cia-controls-the-polish-elites-with-compromising-materials-from-the-communist-era/">CIA</a> controls Polish elites with compromising materials from the Communist era, the West is turning Poland into another ‘<a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/the-west-turns-poland-into-another-reich-for-a-new-drang-nach-osten/">Reich</a>’ for a new ‘Drang nach Osten’, the US wants to drag Warsaw into the Ukraine <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/the-us-wants-to-drag-poland-into-the-war-by-next-year/">war</a> by 2025, and the US <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/non-sovereign-poland-may-be-used-for-a-provocation-to-start-a-nuclear-war-with-russia/">may use Poland</a> to start a nuclear war with Russia.</p> <p>These pro-Kremlin narratives often imply that Western leaders and ‘global elites’ do not care about the Poles. Instead, they are ready to sacrifice them to reach their anti-Russian goals. For instance, one article recently claimed that the American puppet Poland might be pushed to ‘burn’ in a ‘<a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/us-puppet-poland-might-be-pushed-to-burn-in-the-holy-war-against-russia/">holy war</a>’ against Russia.</p> <h3><strong>Poland has imperialist ambitions over Ukraine and Belarus</strong></h3> <p>Another pro-Kremlin disinformation angle trying to smear Poland ahead of its EU presidency was to accuse it of having aggressive and imperialist plans to annex parts of Ukraine and Belarus. If the Kremlin is to be believed, Poland is dreaming of its <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-is-dreaming-of-its-imperial-past-planning-to-overtake-ukraine/">imperial</a> past and wants to rebuild its old <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-wants-to-rebuild-its-empire-with-american-money-and-ukrainian-blood/">empire</a> with American money and Ukrainian blood. Warsaw is moving towards a revival of <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/the-polish-ukrainian-security-agreement-is-another-step-towards-the-revival-of-greater-poland/">Greater Poland</a> and using the Russian military operation as an opportunity to secure the <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-is-using-the-russian-military-operation-to-return-its-eastern-borderlands/">return</a> of its Eastern Borderlands.</p> <p>The Kremlin has also sought to create an impending sense of urgency, falsely claiming that Poland has already started the <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-the-hyena-of-europe-starts-the-partition-of-ukraine/">partition</a> of Ukraine. Supposedly, its troops are moving to the east to <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-is-moving-troops-to-the-east-to-annex-western-ukraine-and-parts-of-belarus/">annex</a> Western Ukraine and parts of Belarus. The Kremlin’s disinformation launderers have then tried to provide ‘evidence’ for these bizarre claims by <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/president-duda-made-polish-territorial-claims-on-belarus-and-ukraine/">deliberately misquoting</a> Polish President Duda or taking the words of Foreign Minister Sikorsky about security in Ukraine <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/polish-foreign-minister-sikorski-starts-talks-about-the-partition-of-ukraine/">completely out of context</a>.</p> <p>As the Kremlin has ramped up its own <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/1-000-and-4-000-days-of-nuclear-sabre-rattling/">nuclear sabre rattling</a>, pro-Kremlin disinformation peddlers have also tried to deflect their own nuclear rhetoric onto Poland, falsely claiming that Warsaw wants to have American <a href="https://euvsdisinfo.eu/report/poland-wants-american-nuclear-weapons-for-the-upcoming-partition-of-ukraine/">nuclear</a> weapons in order to carry out its upcoming partition of Ukraine.</p> <h3><strong>Poland wants nothing but war</strong></h3> <p>Eyeing the <a href="https://www.gov.pl/web/diplomacy/polands-presidency-of-the-council-of-the-eu-in-2025-ministry-of-foreign-affairs-priorities-and-activities2" target="_blank" rel="noopener">security priorities of the Polish EU presidency</a>, the Kremlin has also sought to depict Poland as a warmongering country. It alleges that Warsaw wants nothing but war and is ready to provoke a global conflict.
